newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU offers hand to Turkey, with conditions.
newsitem.headline: EU offers hand to Turkey, with conditions.

text.p: The European Union on Saturday underlined its desire for close links with Turkey, but warned that human rights issues and tensions with EU-member Greece remained an obstacle.
In a communique after a two-day summit, EU leaders said it was important to have both political and economic links with Turkey.
"However...certain serious issues remain to be resolved in the relationship," it said, emphasising "the need for the observance of the highest standards of human rights."
EU presidency Ireland was to host a dinner later on Saturday with Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller.
Relations between Turkey and the EU are strained both by the human rights question, an issue that triggers great concern in the European Parliament, and by Athens' longstanding rivalry with Ankara.
Although a lucrative customs agreement with Turkey came into effect this year, money to help Turkey adjust to it has yet to make it through the web of EU decision making.

Earlier this year, Turkey and Greece nearly came to blows over the sovereignty of some small islands in the Aegaen. The leaders, who have backed Athens, said they were seeking a suitable solution to the problem.
French President Jacques Chirac told reporters he was keen to see Turkey's links reinforced, but admitted that the Ankara-Athens rivarly was a barrier.
"There is tension with Greece which we very much want to improve," he said. "The fact that Greece is inside (the EU) and has a veto doesn't make that easier.
